title: Automation parses human-oriented CLI presentation as a protocol
task: Review an integration that scrapes a command's human-readable table output to drive automation.
context: The CLI output changes wording and column spacing for readability.
Several automation clients parse columns by position.
The CLI already has structured internal result objects.
External automation is expected to grow.
evidence: Minor presentation changes have broken integrations twice.
Human output intentionally omits repeated context that the parser reconstructs heuristically.
tempting_wrong_recommendation: Freeze the human output forever as the machine contract.
Keep improving the scraper because adding another interface is unnecessary.
expected_decision_properties: Distinguish human presentation requirements from machine-contract requirements.
Recommend a structured machine-readable output/API with explicit fields and compatibility policy.
Preserve the human CLI's freedom to optimize readability.
Avoid exposing internal objects directly without defining the machine-facing contract.
unacceptable_reasoning: Whitespace parsing is acceptable because the output currently looks consistent.
The only alternatives are scraping or exposing raw internal objects.
expected_tradeoffs: human presentation freedom vs machine compatibility surface
verification_expectations: Add contract tests for the structured machine representation.
Verify existing human CLI behavior remains usable.
Provide a migration path for current automation clients.
